# Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga (Vb 17)

**ID:** Vb 17
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga
**Title (English, from literature):** Analysis of Minor Matters
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul16.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Following a *mātikā* (matrix), the exposition classifies these unwholesome dhammas numerically into groups of single items, pairs, triads, and up through sets of ten, supplemented by groupings of eighteen and 108 forms of craving [Nyanatiloka 2007; Ñāṇamoli 2010].

**Sources**

- [Sarao and Long 2017] K. T. S. Sarao and Jeffery D. Long (eds.), Buddhism and Jainism (2017) — Identifies Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga as a chapter of the Vibhaṅga and translates the title.
- [Kragh 2006] Ulrich Timme Kragh, The Extant Abhidharma Literature — Describes book 17 as an analysis of small items listing vices.
- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938, repr. 2007) — Details the matrix, numerical structure, and classification of mental defilements and craving.
- [Ñāṇamoli 2010] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli (tr.), The Path of Purification (Visuddhimagga) by Bhadantācariya Buddhaghosa (2010) — Notes the Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga's treatment of the 36 and 108 modes of craving.
